title: Our Planet’s Lungs Are Suffering - Nautilus
gist: A Nature study based on 15 years of aircraft atmospheric sampling suggests the Amazon rainforest may shift from a net carbon sink to a net carbon source. That would weaken a key natural defense against climate change.

insights.claim: A new study published in Nature finds the Amazon rainforest may shift from a net sink to a net source of atmospheric carbon.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Loss of the Amazon sink would raise the pressure on emissions cuts and could lift carbon-market prices and climate-policy stringency.
insights.quote: the Amazon may shift from a net sink to a net source of atmospheric carbon
insights.locator: The Amazon Rainforest is often referred

insights.claim: The Amazon's canopy pulls carbon from the atmosphere and sequesters it, forming an important natural defense against climate change.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Natural sinks underpin carbon budgets; their weakening changes climate-risk assumptions.
insights.locator: The Amazon Rainforest is often referred

insights.claim: The article raises whether the Amazon has reached a dreaded tipping point.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Tipping-point risk is a tail risk for climate-exposed assets and agriculture.
insights.quote: Has the Amazon reached the dreaded tipping point?

insights.claim: Researchers reached their conclusion by analyzing atmospheric samples collected by planes criss-crossing the Amazon over 15 years.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Long-run direct measurement makes the finding more credible than model-only estimates.
insights.locator: A team of climate scientists arrived

insights.claim: Satellite monitoring of the Amazon is hampered by dense cloud cover from evaporating moisture, and ground-based systems are sparse, so direct aircraft sampling was used.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Highlights gaps in satellite-based carbon monitoring, relevant to carbon-credit verification firms.
insights.quote: Satellite-based monitoring is difficult because of the dense blanket of cloud cover generated by evaporating moisture
